verdict.reasoning: Patient reports over the past few days skin has been sore, red, and very itchy: “over the past few days I…noticed my skin is uh, sore and red” and later says “It's very itchy…and dry… I think it's…getting worse, like, the past few days. Way worse.”

Distribution and qualities described: “all over my chest, my hands and arms, and especially inside of the elbows… Which is the, the worst area” and “It's very itchy and, uh, dry, all over my body” and “the areas that are cracked.”
Severe itch and lack of visible scratch marks: “It's very itchy… if I scratch myself, but there's no scratch mark.”
History and worsening episode: Doctor: “you've, got a history of eczema” and patient agrees; patient also states “I think it's…getting worse, like, the past few days. Way worse.”
Patient states: “I, I have asthma” when asked about other medical conditions.
Emollients: “usually I use a a a cream called diprobase. Uh, and in the shower I use something called dermal.”

Hydrocortisone use and OTC antihistamine not helpful: doctor clarifies “So you're using the Hydrocortisone, yeah?” patient: “Yes.” Later, “You've tried the antihistamines and it didn't work… The one over-the-counter… so like cetirizine, yeah?”
Asthma inhaler: Doctor: “The blue inhaler? So you don't, you don't use it everyday, so you just use it on and off, yeah?” Patient: “Yeah. Yeah.” indicating as-needed blue inhaler use.
Doctor asks: “So do you have any allergies to any medication at all?” Patient: “No, no allergies.”
Family history: “in my family, uh, there's hypothyroidism and migraine. My mother has migraine… [and] hypothyroidism… My mother.”

ROS: Doctor: “There's no temperature, no joint pains, yeah? No fever?” (no disagreement from patient). Asthma: “Blue inhalers. But your breathing's all OK, yeah?” Patient: “OK, yeah, yeah. It's only when I have a flare.”

Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare: widespread, dry, cracked, itchy skin and poor response to current measures all described: “It looks like… quite widespread, your eczema” and “It's very itchy and, uh, dry… the areas that are cracked” and hydrocortisone/OTC antihistamine “it's not helping” / “didn't work.”
Intermittent asthma with PRN SABA: “The blue inhaler? So you don't, you don't use it everyday, so you just use it on and off, yeah?” Patient agrees, which is consistent with as-needed SABA use.
Doctor explicitly: “you'd probably need some antihistamines, which I'm going to prescribe… it's called the antihistamine is called Fexofenadine.” This is for her eczema/atopic dermatitis.
Topical steroid plan: “You might probably need a bit more stronger one, like betnovate… we'll try with some Betnovate first… You… have to use it twice a day, for the next couple of weeks.”
Continuation of emollients: “You still need to continue on your, emollients like the dermal soap, and, as well as the, diprovate. Yeah, so you still need to use those, in the interim.”

Education on small amounts and adverse reactions: “it's like one fingertip… This much is, is enough to cover your palms and your - back of your hands… So use that… If… there's no improvement, you need to get back to us. Or, if you have any kind of adverse reaction, like an allergic reaction… you need to get in touch with us… You still need to continue on your, emollients…”

Prescription to Boots: “we're going to send off the prescription to your pharmacy. It looks like Boots on the systems, is that correct?… so i'll send it across to Boot's. And it will be there for collecting.” Same-day collection is implied by “will be there for collecting.”

The transcript confirms current as-needed blue inhaler use but the doctor does not explicitly instruct “continue blue inhaler as needed” in the plan; no asthma management advice is given in the closing plan segment.
Follow-up advice: “If things are getting worse in the next two weeks, call us before hand. Otherwise, wait for two weeks, take the medication and the cream.”
